findings.claim: The fix does not address the root cause of the EPIPE/pipefail interaction; it only changes the reader from `grep -q` to `grep > /dev/null`, which still uses a pipe and can still produce EPIPE if the writer (printf) is killed or the pipe is closed early.
findings.test_or_reason: The ticket's own reproduction (script `5_Project_History/2026-10-23_seatG-18th/evidence/format_gate_select_sim.sh`) shows the read-to-EOF form (`grep "^systemTest/${p}/" > /dev/null`) selected all five packages in 3 of 3 runs, but the fix still uses a pipe; the EPIPE risk is not eliminated, only reduced. The ticket's proposal explicitly mentions a pure-bash `case` match as an alternative, which the PR did not adopt.

findings.claim: The new test does not assert that the gate fails (non-zero exit) when a changed package is dropped; it only checks that the gate exits 0 and reports the expected package count, so a silent skip would still pass the test.
findings.test_or_reason: The ticket's fix shape says 'have the gate fail (not skip) when a package that changed is absent from the checked list', but the test only verifies the exit code is 0 and the count is correct; it does not verify that a dropped package causes a non-zero exit.

findings.claim: The test's fixture packages are created with `format:check` scripts that always exit 0 (except `abc`), so the test cannot detect a package that is silently skipped; the gate would still report '0 skipped' and pass.
findings.test_or_reason: The test's `abc` package is the only one that fails, but it is not used in the large-list cells (cells 1, 2, 4 use `aaa`, `zzz`, and `abc` only in cell 2). The test does not verify that a package with a failing format:check is still checked when the list is large.

findings.claim: The test's `big_list` function generates 2500 paths under `systemTest/zzz/`, but the ticket's measured list was 1,736 paths / 116,058 bytes; the test's list size is not verified to be over 64 KiB in the actual test run, only in the control cell.
findings.test_or_reason: The control cell (line 65-66) checks the list is over 64 KiB, but the actual test cells (1, 2, 4) do not re-check the size; if the list were smaller than 64 KiB, the test would not reproduce the EPIPE condition.

findings.claim: The test's `check` function does not verify that the gate's stderr output is empty or that no 'Broken pipe' line appears, so a regression that still produces EPIPE but happens to select all packages would pass the test.

findings.claim: The fix changes the selection loop but does not update the script's header comment, which still describes the old `grep -q` behavior; the comment now lies about the mechanism.
findings.evidence: systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh:6-11 `# The gate picks each package with `printf '%s\n' "$changed_paths" | grep -q ...` under `set -uo pipefail`. grep -q exits at its FIRST match; when the list is bigger than the pipe buffer (64 KiB) printf is still writing, gets EPIPE, and pipefail turns the pipeline into "no match". The package is then neither checked nor skipped, and the gate still prints "0 skipped". The fix reads the list to EOF (grep without -q, output to /dev/null).`
